text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEnvironmentOur Planet’s Lungs Are SufferingHas the Amazon reached the dreaded tipping point?JCBy Jake Currie3:00 PM CDT on October 29, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThe Amazon Rainforest is often referred to as the “lungs of the planet” because its lush canopy “inhales” carbon dioxide and “exhales” oxygen. This breathing pattern is part of an important natural defense against climate change, pulling carbon from the atmosphere and sequestering it, but that might be changing. According to a new study published in Nature, the Amazon may shift from a net sink to a net source of atmospheric carbon.A team of climate scientists arrived at that conclusion after analyzing atmospheric samples taken by planes criss-crossing the skies over the Amazon for 15 years. Satellite-based monitoring is difficult because of the dense blanket of cloud cover generated by evaporating moisture and ground-based systems are few and far between.
